observations: Industrial-looking yard/workshop scene with multiple metal fabricated units.
A large rotating perforated drum (cylindrical sieve) sits in a green-framed stand, consistent with a separator/sieving unit.
Two boxy metal housings with chimney-like vents stand in the middle, likely cracker/separator housings.
A funnel-shaped green hopper sits at right, feeding into a flywheel/pulley wheel assembly.
No diesel engine is clearly visible or distinguishable in the frame; the round wheel could be a pulley for a belt-driven motor but no engine body is shown.
Watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI / JESSICA NNANNA' overlays the image, obscuring some detail.
Ground is cluttered with scrap metal, cardboard, and loose parts, suggesting a fabrication yard rather than a clean showroom.
No brand plates, model numbers, or engine nameplates are legible anywhere in the photo.

risks.proof: A clear photo showing the full diesel engine with visible make/model plate and its connection to the machine.

risks.risk: Machine may not be functional (cracker/separator mechanism could be rusted, jammed, or missing internal parts).
risks.proof: A video of the machine running, processing palm kernels end to end.

risks.risk: Visible rust on the drum and housings may indicate long disuse or corrosion damage affecting lifespan.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the drum interior and housing welds/joints.

risks.risk: Set may be incomplete (cracker and separator could be sold as two separate units, not one combined machine).
risks.proof: Wide shot showing both units fully, with seller confirming unit boundaries and what is included in the sale.
risks.if_unproven: priced as separator unit only, cracker unverified

risks.risk: Electrical/mechanical wiring, belts, or missing parts (scrap clutter nearby suggests disassembly).
risks.proof: Photo of complete belt/pulley assembly and any control panel or switchgear.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the diesel engine itself, including any nameplate with make, model, and horsepower.
A video of the machine running (cracking and separating kernels) to confirm functionality.
Close-up photos of the drum interior, welds, and any wear points.
Confirmation and photo showing exactly what is included in the sale (cracker unit, separator unit, engine, belts, hopper) as one lot.
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type as a palm kernel cracker and separator setup, but the claimed diesel engine is not visible and functionality cannot be confirmed, so it must be priced at worst case (no confirmed working engine, unverified mechanical condition).
